accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EYFS 2024 ELG The Natural World, the KS1 Year 2 programme of study Living things and their habitats (habitats to which they are suited, basic needs, microhabitats) and NGSS K-ESS3-1. Biology checked against standard references: fish take oxygen from water through gills, earthworms breathe through moist skin so need damp soil, woodlice (terrestrial isopods) lose water easily and show humidity and light preferences in choice-chamber investigations, rabbits shelter from foxes in burrows, and a raised nest keeps eggs warm and away from ground predators. The adult text says the 7 of 8 woodlouse result is a model and real chambers show most, not all.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented early-years ideas about habitats: any animal can live anywhere (prediction In a nest for the fish, tag any), animals pick homes for fun or looks rather than needs (tag fun), mixing up whose home is whose (tag mix, plus refusals in the matching step that say why, e.g. a fish out of water cannot breathe), and the belief that minibeasts like sunny dry places (prediction The bright, dry side, tag dry). The nest step targets the idea that a nest anywhere is equally safe.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaghome is a habitat model: animals are carried into four habitat boxes, a log is lifted to reveal a microhabitat and eight woodlice walk a split choice chamber, a blackbird nest is placed on the ground or a branch before a fox walks past, and a bug home attracts minibeasts only from dark, damp materials. flagbaby (animals and babies) and flagliving (living or not) have no habitat or needs model, and the 30 percent shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees the reason before reading it: a wrong drop is refused with the need it breaks (a worm needs damp soil, or its skin dries out), the chamber result is counted on screen (7 of 8 chose dark and damp), the fox reaches only the ground nest, and a plastic bag brings no minibeasts while a log brings two. Each done message states the idea after the evidence is on the canvas.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: In a nest or In a burrow for the fish (refused in the matching step), The bright, dry side or half and half for woodlice (7 of 8 go dark and damp), and On the ground for the nest (the fox reaches it). A.reveal repeats the child's own guess with the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions (worm, fish, woodlice, nest, rabbit) with each wrong answer tagged: dry (worms and woodlice dry out in the sun, they need dark damp places), mix (that is another animal's home, with all four pairings named), any (a home must give what the animal needs, like water, food or a safe place) and fun (animals do not pick homes for fun). Answers rotate so the right one is not always first.

readability.evidence: Family audience: kid paragraphs are short read-aloud sentences (A rabbit digs a hole in the ground. It is called a burrow.) and pass the family kid limit; the adult text uses the exact Year 2 and EYFS terms habitat, microhabitat, shelter, basic needs and suited, explains minibeast as an early-years word, and passes the adult limit. Lab labels are one or two words (Pond, Nest, Burrow, Soil).

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate passed and overlap with every other lesson, including Animals and their babies and Living and not living, is under 12 percent. Kid paragraphs each add one habitat and how it helps; adult paragraphs give the curriculum links, the key words, named mistakes with the gill and skin-breathing caution, and the lab outline with the model caveat.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark after every Show me: the four habitat boxes fill a 2 by 2 grid with 34 px animals, the lifted log no longer covers the heading, the choice chamber halves are labelled bright, dry and dark, damp with the count underneath, the safe-nest message sits in the grass clear of the tree, and the bug-home kit tiles fit four across. Every action has a full-width button twin.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, all 5 Show me tasks completed and the challenge showed. Matching works by pick-then-place buttons as well as drag, the canvas aria-label speaks each result (Worm lives in the soil. Damp soil keeps its skin wet.), and the chamber uses words and counts, not colour alone.
